database_summary: This is a movie-centric analytical schema (SQLite) containing a Movie master table and several descriptor tables (Genre, Language, Country, Location, Person) plus many many-to-many bridge tables (prefixed M_ and M_*) that link movies to genres, languages, countries, locations, cast, directors and producers. The schema is read-oriented and represents descriptive attributes and membership relationships (no explicit timestamps or temporal/versioning columns). Row counts show a relatively small Movie fact set (~3.5k) with larger person and cast association tables. Many joins between Movie and bridge tables are one-to-many and can multiply rows; bridge tables are the natural place to filter by membership.

accepted.name: movies_core
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  MID,
  title,
  year,
  rating,
  num_votes
FROM Movie
accepted.description: Normalized movie master rows with canonical key and key measures exposed. Use this as the base movie relation for joins, filtering, and aggregations. | Use for: Top-rated movies by year; Movies with high vote counts; Joining movies to genres/countries/languages/people

accepted.name: movie_genres
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  M_Genre.MID AS MID,
  M_Genre.GID AS GID,
  Genre.Name AS Name
FROM M_Genre
LEFT JOIN Genre ON M_Genre.GID = Genre.GID
accepted.description: Denormalized mapping of movies to genre names. One row per movie-genre pair, preserving movie and genre identifiers and descriptive genre Name. Use when filtering or aggregating by genre. | Use for: Count movies per genre; List genres for a given movie; Top-rated movies within each genre

accepted.name: movie_languages
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  M_Language.MID AS MID,
  M_Language.LAID AS LAID,
  Language.Name AS Name
FROM M_Language
LEFT JOIN Language ON M_Language.LAID = Language.LAID
accepted.description: Denormalized mapping of movies to language names. One row per movie-language pair, preserving movie and language identifiers and descriptive language Name. | Use for: Movies by language; Counts of movies per language; Filter movies by language and year

accepted.name: movie_countries
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  M_Country.MID AS MID,
  M_Country.CID AS CID,
  Country.Name AS Name
FROM M_Country
LEFT JOIN Country ON M_Country.CID = Country.CID
accepted.description: Denormalized mapping of movies to country names. One row per movie-country pair, preserving movie and country identifiers and descriptive country Name. | Use for: Films produced in a given country; Count movies per country; Top-rated movies by country

accepted.name: movie_locations
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  M_Location.MID AS MID,
  M_Location.LID AS LID,
  Location.Name AS Name
FROM M_Location
LEFT JOIN Location ON M_Location.LID = Location.LID
accepted.description: Denormalized mapping of movies to location names. One row per movie-location pair, preserving movie and location identifiers and descriptive Location Name. | Use for: Movies filmed in a given location; Count filming locations per movie; Filter movies by location and year

accepted.name: movie_people_roles
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  M_Cast.MID AS MID,
  M_Cast.PID AS PID,
  Person.Name AS Name,
  'cast' AS role
FROM M_Cast
LEFT JOIN Person ON M_Cast.PID = Person.PID
UNION ALL
SELECT
  M_Director.MID AS MID,
  M_Director.PID AS PID,
  Person.Name AS Name,
  'director' AS role
FROM M_Director
LEFT JOIN Person ON M_Director.PID = Person.PID
UNION ALL
SELECT
  M_Producer.MID AS MID,
  M_Producer.PID AS PID,
  Person.Name AS Name,
  'producer' AS role
FROM M_Producer
LEFT JOIN Person ON M_Producer.PID = Person.PID
accepted.description: Unioned relation of movie-person-role membership across cast, directors, and producers. One row per (movie, person, role) preserving PID and Name and the role label which helps filter by role without joining multiple bridge tables. | Use for: List cast/director/producer for a movie; Find movies for a given person and role; Aggregate counts of distinct people by role per movie

accepted.name: movie_genre_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  M_Genre.MID AS MID,
  COUNT(DISTINCT M_Genre.GID) AS genre_count,
  group_concat(DISTINCT Genre.Name) AS genre_list
FROM M_Genre
LEFT JOIN Genre ON M_Genre.GID = Genre.GID
GROUP BY M_Genre.MID
accepted.description: Per-movie aggregated counts of how many genres are associated with each movie and a concatenated genre list (when SQLite group_concat is available). Useful to filter multi-genre movies or join a compact genre summary to Movie. | Use for: Find movies with multiple genres; Show genre summary alongside movie metrics; Filter movies by presence/absence of genre membership counts

accepted.name: movie_person_counts_by_role
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  MID,
  SUM(CASE WHEN role = 'cast' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cast_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN role = 'director' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS director_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN role = 'producer' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS producer_count
FROM (
  SELECT MID, PID, 'cast' AS role FROM M_Cast
  UNION ALL
  SELECT MID, PID, 'director' AS role FROM M_Director
  UNION ALL
  SELECT MID, PID, 'producer' AS role FROM M_Producer
) sub
GROUP BY MID
accepted.description: Per-movie counts of distinct people by role (cast, director, producer). Produces one row per movie with separate measure columns for each role count, useful for filtering or correlating movie measures with team sizes. | Use for: Compare movies by size of cast or crew; Filter movies with no directors or multiple producers; Correlate team sizes with ratings

accepted.name: movies_rating_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  MID,
  title,
  year,
  rating,
  num_votes,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY rating DESC, num_votes DESC) AS year_rating_rank
FROM Movie
accepted.description: Per-year ranking of movies by rating then num_votes. Exposes a dense rank so downstream queries can select top-K per year by applying a rank <= K predicate. Year is preserved as-is (text). | Use for: Top-K movies per year by rating; Find where a movie ranks within its release year; Yearly leaderboards by rating

accepted.name: movies_running_votes
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  MID,
  title,
  year,
  rating,
  num_votes,
  SUM(num_votes) OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY rating DESC, num_votes DESC ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS year_votes_cume
FROM Movie
accepted.description: Within-year cumulative sum of num_votes ordered by rating descending. Useful to analyze how vote accumulation relates to ranking within a year or to compute percentiles via joins. | Use for: Share of votes captured by top-N movies in a year; Cumulative distribution of votes by rating within a year
